basic_commands.title: Welcome to Python! 🐍
basic_commands.description: Learn your first commands and start programming!

steps.title: Hello, Programmer!
steps.content: You are about to learn Python, one of the coolest programming languages in the world! Python is used to create games, apps, robots, and even teach artificial intelligence!

steps.title: Your First Command: print()
steps.content: The print() command is like a megaphone for the computer. Everything you put inside the parentheses will appear on the screen!

steps.title: Texts Need Quotes
steps.content: When you write text in Python, you need to put it inside quotes. It can be double quotes " " or single quotes ' '. This way Python knows it's a text!

steps.title: Python Knows Math!
steps.content: You can use Python like a magic calculator! If you put an equation inside print(), it calculates and shows the result.

steps.title: Comments: Secret Notes
steps.content: Lines that start with # are comments. Python ignores them! It's like writing a note just for you or other programmers.

steps.title: Ready to Start!
steps.content: You learned the basics! Now it's time to practice. Remember: print() shows on the screen, texts stay in quotes, and # makes comments. Good luck!

numbers.title: Magic Calculator 🔢
numbers.description: Learn to perform incredible calculations with Python!

steps.title: Python: Your Personal Calculator
steps.content: Python is very good at math! You can do any calculation with it, from the simplest to the most complicated.

steps.title: Addition and Subtraction
steps.content: Use + to add and - to subtract. It's just like school math!

steps.title: Multiplication and Division
steps.content: Use * to multiply and / to divide. Careful: the result of division always has a decimal point!

steps.title: Integer Division and Remainder
steps.content: // divides and ignores decimals. % gives the remainder of the division. They are super useful!

steps.title: Power: The Super Power!
steps.content: Use ** to raise a number to a power. 2 ** 3 means 2 × 2 × 2!

steps.title: Math Wizard!
steps.content: Now you know how to do any calculation in Python! Practice a lot and become a number wizard!

variables.title: Magic Boxes 📦
variables.description: Learn to store information to use later!

steps.title: What is a Variable?
steps.content: A variable is like a magic box! You give it a name and can store anything inside: numbers, texts, lists...

steps.title: Creating a Variable
steps.content: To create a variable, write the name, an equal sign (=), and the value. It's like putting a label on the box!

steps.title: Variables Can Change
steps.content: The cool thing is you can change the value whenever you want! That's why it's called "variable" - the value can vary.

steps.title: Data Types
steps.content: Python has 4 basic data types: int (integer numbers), str (texts), float (decimal numbers), and bool (true/false).

steps.title: Discovering the Type
steps.content: Use type() to find out the type of any variable. It's like asking: "What kind of thing are you?"

steps.title: Converting Types
steps.content: Sometimes you need to convert one type to another. Use int(), str(), and float() for this!

steps.title: Joining Texts
steps.content: Use + to join texts! But beware: to join text with a number, first convert with str().

steps.title: Rules for Names
steps.content: Variable names can have letters, numbers, and _. But they cannot start with a number and cannot have spaces!

steps.title: You Learned Variables!
steps.content: Now you know how to store information, the 4 basic types, and how to convert between them! This is super important!

conditions.title: Making Choices 🔀
conditions.description: Learn to make the computer make decisions!

steps.title: Decisions in Everyday Life
steps.content: Every day you make decisions: "IF it's raining, I'll take an umbrella". The computer can do this too with the if command!

steps.title: The if Command
steps.content: if means "se" in Portuguese. We use it to ask questions and run code only if the answer is true.

steps.title: Comparing Values
steps.content: We can compare values with: == (equal), != (different), > (greater), < (less), >= (greater or equal), <= (less or equal)

steps.title: Else: The Plan B
steps.content: Use else to say what to do when the condition is false. It's your plan B!

steps.title: Multiple Options: elif
steps.content: elif ("else if") allows testing multiple conditions. It's like having many doors to choose from!

steps.title: AND: Two Conditions Together
steps.content: Use and when TWO conditions need to be true. Both must be true!

steps.title: OR: One or the Other
steps.content: Use or when AT LEAST ONE condition needs to be true. One is enough!

steps.title: NOT: Inverting
steps.content: Use not to invert a condition. True becomes False and False becomes True!

steps.title: IN: Checking with in
steps.content: Use in to check if something is inside a list or text. Super useful!

steps.title: Master of Decisions!
steps.content: Now you master if, else, elif, and, or, not, and in! Your programs can make complex decisions!

loops.title: Repeating Magic 🔄
loops.description: Learn to repeat commands without writing everything again!

steps.title: Why Repeat?
steps.content: Imagine writing "Hi!" 100 times... Tiring, right? With loops, you write it once and the computer repeats it as many times as you want!

steps.title: The for Loop
steps.content: for repeats a block of code a specific number of times. It's like a carousel that spins several times!

steps.title: Understanding range()
steps.content: range(5) generates numbers from 0 to 4 (5 numbers). range(1, 6) generates from 1 to 5. The last number never enters!

steps.title: Looping through Lists
steps.content: You can also use for to iterate over each item in a list!

steps.title: The while Loop
steps.content: while repeats WHILE a condition is true. Be careful not to create an infinite loop!

steps.title: break: Emergency Brake!
steps.content: Use break to STOP the loop immediately! It's like hitting the emergency brake.

steps.title: continue: Skip a Turn
steps.content: Use continue to SKIP to the next iteration of the loop, without executing the rest of the code.

steps.title: Loop Master!
steps.content: You learned for, while, break, and continue! Now you can control loops like a pro!

lists.title: Organizing Everything 📜
lists.description: Learn to store many things in a single list!

steps.title: What is a List?
steps.content: Lists are like backpacks where you store several things together! It can have numbers, texts, or even other lists inside.

steps.title: Creating a List
steps.content: Use square brackets [ ] and separate items with commas. Simple as that!

steps.title: Accessing Items
steps.content: To get an item, use the index in square brackets. REMEMBER: In Python, we count starting from 0!

steps.title: Slicing the List
steps.content: Use [start:end] to get a piece of the list. The end is not included! It's like slicing a cake.

steps.title: Adding Items
steps.content: Use .append() to add an item to the end of the list!

steps.title: Removing Items
steps.content: Use .pop() to remove the last one, or .remove() to remove by value.

steps.title: Sorting the List
steps.content: Use .sort() to put the items in order!

steps.title: Counting Items
steps.content: len() tells you how many items are in the list. Super useful!

steps.title: Master of Lists!
steps.content: You master lists! Create, access, slice, add, remove, and sort. Lists are essential in programming!

steps.title: What is a Function?
steps.content: Functions are like cake recipes! You write it once and can use it as many times as you want. Just "call" it by name.

steps.title: Creating a Function
steps.content: Use def to define a function. After the name, put parentheses and a colon. The function code is indented!

steps.title: Parameters: The Inputs
steps.content: Parameters are information you pass to the function. They are like the ingredients of a recipe!

steps.title: return: The Output
steps.content: return gives back a result from the function. It's like the postman delivering the answer!

steps.title: Multiple Parameters
steps.content: You can have as many parameters as you want! Separate them with commas.

steps.title: Default Parameters
steps.content: You can give a default value to a parameter! If no one passes it, use the default. It's like a plan B.

steps.title: Scope: Local Variables
steps.content: Variables created INSIDE a function only exist there! They "die" when the function ends. They are called local variables.

steps.title: Function Creator!
steps.content: You master functions! Create, parameters, return, default values, and scope. Your functions will make your code amazing!

strings.title: Master of Words 📝
strings.description: Learn to manipulate texts like a pro!

steps.title: What are Strings?
steps.content: Strings are texts in Python. Everything inside quotes is a string, be it a letter, a word, or a whole book!

steps.title: Joining Texts
steps.content: Use + to join (concatenate) strings. You can create personalized messages!

steps.title: f-strings: The Modern Way
steps.content: f-strings are easier! Put f before the quotes and use {variable} inside the text.

steps.title: String Methods
steps.content: Strings have superpowers! Use .upper() for uppercase, .lower() for lowercase.

steps.title: Breaking Text: split()
steps.content: split() divides the text into a list! By default, it cuts at spaces, but you can choose the separator.

steps.title: Joining List: join()
steps.content: join() is the opposite of split! It joins a list of words into a single text.

steps.title: Slicing Strings
steps.content: You can get parts of a string using [start:end]. It's like cutting a piece of cake!

steps.title: Master of Strings!
steps.content: You master texts! Join, separate, slice, transform... Strings are essential in every program!

steps.title: Programs that Talk!
steps.content: Until now, your programs only spoke. But with input() they can listen! It's like giving a microphone to the user.

steps.title: The input() Command
steps.content: input() makes the program stop and wait for the user to type something. Whatever is typed is stored in a variable.

steps.title: input() Always Gives Text!
steps.content: CAREFUL! Even if the user types 42, input() returns "42" (text). To do math, you need to convert it!

steps.title: int() - Converting to Number
steps.content: Use int() to transform text into an integer number. This way you can do math!

steps.title: float() - Numbers with Point
steps.content: For decimal numbers (like 1.75), use float(). IMPORTANT: In Python, we use a POINT (.) and not a comma for decimals!

steps.title: Interactive Programs!
steps.content: Now you know how to make programs that talk to the user! Remember: input() gives text, use int() or float() for numbers.

dictionaries.title: Magic Phonebook 📚
dictionaries.description: Learn to organize data with keys and values!

steps.title: What is a Dictionary?
steps.content: Imagine a phonebook: you look for the NAME (key) and find the PHONE (value). Dictionaries work like this!

steps.title: Keys and Values
steps.content: Each information in the dictionary has a key (the name) and a value (the information).

steps.title: Accessing Values
steps.content: To get a value, use the key in square brackets. It's like looking in the phonebook!

steps.title: Adding New Keys
steps.content: To add something new, just assign it! The key is created automatically.

steps.title: Lists vs Dictionaries
steps.content: Lists use indexes (0, 1, 2...). Dictionaries use names as keys. Use dictionaries when names make more sense!

steps.title: Master of Dictionaries!
steps.content: Dictionaries are super useful for organizing data clearly. Everything has a name!

error_handling.title: Hunting Bugs! 🛡️
error_handling.description: Learn to protect your programs against errors!

steps.title: What are Errors?
steps.content: Sometimes the program encounters problems: dividing by zero, converting invalid text... Python stops and shows an error.

steps.title: Errors Stop the Program!
steps.content: Without protection, any error makes the whole program stop. But we can avoid this!

steps.title: try/except to the Rescue!
steps.content: Put the "dangerous" code inside try. If an error occurs, the except takes care of it!

steps.title: Program Continues!
steps.content: With try/except, even if there's an error, the program doesn't stop. It continues after the except!

steps.title: Types of Error
steps.content: Each error has a name: ZeroDivisionError, ValueError, TypeError... You can handle each one differently!

steps.title: Robust Programs!
steps.content: Now your programs can handle problems without breaking! Use try/except whenever something could go wrong.

files.title: Files of Knowledge 📂
files.description: Learn to read and write real text files!

steps.title: Saving Data Forever
steps.content: When the program closes, variables disappear. To save data forever, we use files on the computer!

steps.title: Writing to Files
steps.content: We use with open("name.txt", "w") to open a file in write mode ("w" for write).

steps.title: Reading Files
steps.content: We use the "r" (read) mode to read the contents of a file!

steps.title: Master of Files!
steps.content: Now you know how to save scores, diaries, and reports in real files!

steps.title: What are Modules?
steps.content: Modules are ready-made toolboxes created by other programmers so you don't have to reinvent the wheel!

steps.title: random Module
steps.content: Use import random to make draws and games with random numbers!

steps.title: math Module
steps.content: Use import math for super calculations like square root and pi!

steps.title: Module Summoner!
steps.content: With import you have thousands of incredible tools at your fingertips!

oop_basics.title: The Art of Objects 🧙‍♂️
oop_basics.description: Create molds and characters with Classes and Objects!

steps.title: Molds (Classes) and Objects
steps.content: A Class is the recipe or mold for a cookie. The Object is the real cookie you create!

steps.title: Creating a Class with class
steps.content: We use class ClassName: and the __init__(self) method to initialize the characteristics.

steps.title: Actions (Methods)
steps.content: Methods are functions created inside the class that give superpowers to objects!

steps.title: Architect of Objects!
steps.content: You learned Object-Oriented Programming, the pillar of almost all modern games and software!

pythonic.title: Magic Shortcuts ⚡
pythonic.description: Write clean, fast, and powerful code!

steps.title: Elegant Code (Pythonic)
steps.content: In Python, we like clean and readable code. List Comprehension allows creating lists in a single line!

steps.title: List Comprehension
steps.content: Instead of using a 4-line for, summarize everything in [expression for item in list]!

steps.title: Pythonic Sprinter!
steps.content: Your programs are now super elegant and professional!

turtle_art.title: Art & Turtle Studio 🎨
turtle_art.description: Draw geometric shapes and animations on the screen!

steps.title: Drawing with Code
steps.content: With the turtle module, you control a little turtle pen that draws on the screen as it moves!

steps.title: Main Commands
steps.content: forward(steps) moves forward, right(ang) and left(ang) turn the turtle!

steps.title: Code Artist!
steps.content: Now you can create incredible stars, spirals, and mandalas!

data_science.title: Data & AI Lab 🤖
data_science.description: Analyze statistics and discover intelligence in data!

steps.title: The Power of Data
steps.content: Artificial Intelligence learns by analyzing millions of data. In Python, we use functions like sum(), max(), min(), and len().

steps.title: Calculating the Average
steps.content: The average of a list of numbers is calculated by dividing the total sum by the number of items!

steps.title: Data Scientist!
steps.content: You now know how to extract insights and intelligence from numbers!

web_api.title: The Internet Web & APIs 🌐
web_api.description: Connect your code to live real-world data!

steps.title: What is an API?
steps.content: APIs allow your Python code to talk to the internet to get the weather, news, currencies, and much more!

steps.title: Reading JSON Data
steps.content: Web responses come in JSON, which we access exactly like dictionaries in Python!

steps.title: Master of the Web!
steps.content: Your programs are now connected to the whole world!
